transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-25
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Samira (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Diego (Redwood CSM), Maria (Brightline Legal), Tom (Brightline Procurement), Priya (Brightline CTO), Alex (Brightline Security)

[00:00] Samira: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call - you'll see Ethan and I from Redwood, Diego's here for onboarding context. Maria, Tom, Priya, Alex, can you hear us?
[00:10] Maria: Yes, loud and clear. Thanks.
[00:13] Tom: Yep, we're good.
[00:15] Priya: Hi all.
[00:18] Samira: Great. The objective for today is to map out your vendor approval path and close the open SLA items so procurement has a clear sign-off pathway. We'll also cover the DPA/MSA redline expectations.
[00:30] Priya: To kick off, from engineering side the big things are data residency — we need EU-only processing for a subset of PII — and KMS control, ideally customer-managed keys. Also latency SLAs for our real-time product.
[00:42] Ethan: Got it. For KMS we support both customer-managed keys via bring-your-own-key and Redwood-managed. There's an HSM-backed KMS option for Private. For hosted we can offer envelope encryption with KMS integrations.
[00:55] Alex: When you say Private, do you mean full private deployment in our VPC or Redwood Private with a managed control plane? We need to know key custody implications.
[01:05] Ethan: Good question. We have two options: Redwood Private with customer-controlled VPC peering (control plane hosted but data plane in your network) which allows BYOK, or an on-prem package where both control and data plane live in your infra. The on-prem gives you full key custody.
[01:20] Maria: From legal, the DPA needs a clamped definition of subprocessors and data flow diagrams. Also, we flagged the indemnity clause and want to propose a liability cap tied to fees.
[01:33] Samira: Makes sense. For subprocessors we can provide a listing and commit to 30-day notice for additions, that's in our standard. Liability cap we can discuss — our typical is 1x annual fees but we can take notes on your proposed language.
[01:46] Tom: Procurement will want to see clear SLAs mapped to credits and a remedy timeline. We have internal policy that requires at least 99.9% uptime for production workloads and measurable 99th percentile latency figures. How flexible is Redwood on credits vs service credits vs termination?
[02:05] Ethan: Our SLA table typically specifies uptime targets per deployment type: hosted API SLA is 99.9% (with credits), Dedicated higher-tier contracts offer pre-negotiated latencies and a faster incident response SLO. For termination we usually allow cure periods; we can discuss escalations. I can attach our SLA matrix after this call.
[02:20] Priya: For latency numbers, can you show 99th percentile for 512-token gen and for chat workloads? We have spikes during batch window and need to understand tail latency behavior.
[02:35] Ethan: Yes, we'll provide those graphs. Note that tail latency varies by model and quantization. For Dedicated pools we can give more consistent 99th perc. For hosted there can be variance — but we have routing policies and fallbacks to maintain availability.
[02:50] Maria: Also, security evidence — SOC 2 report, pen test summary, vuln management cadence. We have a hold point in our legal process until security artifacts are uploaded.
[03:03] Diego: We can share our most recent SOC 2 type II and a redacted pen test executive summary. The security pack is usually in the security binder we send to prospects.
[03:12] Alex: Will that include retention and deletion guarantees? We need explicit statement around KV cache and persisted logs.
[03:19] Ethan: Yes — we can document token-level retention defaults. For Private deployments you control logs; for hosted we provide configurable retention policies and can sign a data retention appendix.
[03:30] Tom: There's also pricing gating — procurement needs to know commit tiers, overage rates, and egress fees. Our legal team tends to push to a committed model to get locked-in pricing.
[03:45] Samira: We've proposed a committed reserved capacity for Dedicated with predictable throughput and discounts. We'll share a committed pricing worksheet that maps to throughput and expected unit economics.
[03:55] Priya: What's the minimum commitment? Our finance prefers quarterly commitments that can be scaled.
[04:03] Samira: We typically have monthly and annual reserved tiers; we can propose a 3-month pilot with a conversion path to annual reserved if that helps procurement.
[04:15] Maria: On the MSA redlines, we will send a set of DPA-specific edits — primarily around subprocessors, data residency, and liability. How do you prefer to receive redlines? Word? PDF?
[04:27] Samira: Word with track changes is ideal. We'll put inline comments and a short change-log table.
[04:32] Maria: Okay we'll get that out by Monday.
[04:36] Alex: A question on audit logs — do we get token-level auditability and exportable traces for requests tied to customer tokens? We might require that to satisfy internal auditors.
[04:48] Ethan: Yes, we provide request-level logs for dedicated and private deployments. For hosted we provide aggregated logs by default and can enable request-level auditing for higher tiers. Export formats are JSON/CSV.
[05:00] Tom: On the procurement calendar side, our committee meets next on 2025-12-04; we'd like pricing and SLA positions in by 12/01. If we can get the MSA redlines and the SLA matrix by 11/28-11/29 that would fit our review window.
[05:15] Samira: We'll aim to hit those dates. Ethan, Diego, can you commit to getting artifacts uploaded?
[05:21] Ethan: Yes, I'll upload benchmarks and SLA spreadsheets by 11/27.
[05:25] Diego: I'll prepare the security binder and SOC2 by 11/28.
[05:29] Priya: Another technical point — can Redwood support private model variants or only public/open models? For regulatory reasons we may want a trimmed model deployed in our VPC.
[05:42] Ethan: We support model pinning and can onboard private model artifacts for Private/on-prem deployments. There's a model onboarding checklist and security review; we can run that as part of the pilot.
[05:54] Maria: Regarding indemnity and liability, we will propose language limiting our exposure but also asking for carve-outs for gross negligence. Is that typically acceptable?
[06:03] Samira: Gross negligence carve-outs are standard language. We can take your proposed clause to legal, but we generally try to keep liability caps proportionate to fees and carve-outs for willful misconduct.
[06:16] Tom: One last procurement item — do you have any list of references from financial services customers? That helps with internal risk committees.
[06:25] Diego: We can share anonymized references and case studies — I will pre-clear a short list that demonstrates regulated-financial usage.
[06:33] Priya: Ok, on timeline, if we get redlines 11/28 and your artifacts 11/27, is it realistic to be in contracting by mid-December?
[06:44] Samira: Yes, if there are no heavy commercial changes. Our typical courtroom — sorry — our typical path is redlines, security review, procurement pricing approval, then counteroffers. Mid-December contracting is feasible.
[06:58] Maria: We'll put internal reviewers on standby for the week of 11/30.
[07:03] Alex: A minor technical question — does Redwood support BYO HSM integrations via cloud KMS (AWS KMS, GCP Cloud KMS) or must we use Redwood's provider?
[07:14] Ethan: We integrate with AWS KMS and GCP KMS for envelope encryption. For full HSM BYOK you usually need the Private/on-prem deployment to meet strict key custody requirements.
[07:26] Samira: Let's capture that as an action item — we'll mark which KMS options are available per deployment type in the security pack.
[07:33] Tom: Procurement also asked about termination assistance — data extraction timelines after contract end. Can you commit to a minimum export window and deletion certificate?
[07:45] Diego: Yes, we have an offboarding runbook that includes data export within 30 days and deletion confirmation. For Private deployments you control retention directly. We can include timelines in the DPA appendix.
[07:58] Maria: Are there any export control or cross-border transfer clauses in the standard MSA we should be aware of?
[08:06] Samira: The standard MSA covers data transfers in the DPA and we have region-specific addenda for EU data residency. If you need a dedicated EU instance or on-prem we can map that.
[08:20] Priya: For the pilot, we'd like a 4-week eval with a capped spend and predictable throughput. During that time we want a runbook for incident triage and RFCs to the SE.
[08:33] Ethan: We can set up a 4-week pilot with a capped reserved capacity and a biweekly check-in. We'll provide an incident triage template and an escalation contact list.
[08:44] Tom: Will pilot usage count toward a reserved commitment if we convert?
[08:49] Samira: We can credit pilot usage against the first-month commit under agreed conversion terms. We'll document that in the commercial term sheet.
[08:58] Maria: Ok, sounds good. Next steps for legal: we'll circulate MSA+DPA redlines Monday, and procurement will need a pricing worksheet to match against our internal models.
[09:09] Samira: Understood. To summarize next steps: Samira sends change-log + MSA export, Ethan shares benchmark and SLA graphs, Diego uploads SOC2 and security pack, Alex sets SecOps follow-up. Tom confirms procurement calendar.
[09:23] Priya: Anything else we should cover?
[09:26] Tom: Not from procurement.
[09:28] Alex: Minor note — our security team will want to test an on-prem demo in a later phase.
[09:33] Ethan: We support a technical ride-along for on-prem; we'll scope that after contract.
[09:38] Samira: Great. Thanks everyone. We'll send the artifacts and follow up with a SecOps deep-dive invite.
[09:44] Maria: Thanks all.
[09:46] Tom: Thanks.
[09:47] (end)

Notes on transcript: occasional ASR mis-words in names; timestamps approximate. Some speaker labels simplified.
